newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices extend gains but remain below week high.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices extend gains but remain below week high.

text.p: Oil prices extended day-earlier gains on Friday but did not manage to make up all the ground lost in a ferocious mid-week selloff sparked by the resumption of Iraqi oil exports.
At 1600 GMT, January futures of world benchmark Brent Blend crude stood up 36 cents at $22.88 a barrel.
Since Thursday, Brent has gained about 70 cents but the recovery is seen as only modest after a fall of $1.50 earlier in the week.
This week, Iraqi oil flowed to the market for the first time since 1990 when Baghdad was hit by with a United Nations' trade ban after it invaded Kuwait.
After months of wangling between Baghdad and the U.N., a plan allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to pay for food and medicines got the green light this week.
Although only a handful of contracts have been signed, traders reckon Iraq will eventually ship about 500,000-600,000 barrels of oil daily to the market.
Forecasts for colder weather in some parts of the United States, the world's largest heating oil consumer, lent some bullishness to the market on Friday, traders said.
Though there have been some stock building in recent weeks as refineries work overtime to build supplies before bitter weather sets it, inventories remain below 1995 levels.
